incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1890012345 - GPU pool saturation detected for region-us-west-2. Autoscaler observed sustained queue growth > 3m. Token-bucket throttle firing on tier=standard.

maria.ops: seeing lots of 429s hitting customers on /v1/generate, started at ~1890012330. Customers report partial responses and retries.

jordan: confirmed. Logs show token_bucket_allow=false for many requests. Token refill rate at 0.8 rps for standard tier, burst=2. Queue length per hotpath worker is ~120.

devon: autoscaler hasn't added nodes in last 10m despite queue > 100. Metrics show scale_decisions=blocked by policy "max_per_zone=2" - we hit configured cap.

sre-jon: passing to oncall. @maria.ops you're on-call - can you confirm whether we should lift per-zone cap?

maria.ops: on it. Quick check: max_per_zone was reduced in rollout earlier today (PR 7842) to limit cost. That change didn't consider sudden burst patterns.

beth: customer impact: three customers report degraded latency and errors; severity appears medium->high since some automated workflows are failing.

jordan: attaching a short log snippet: ```
[1890012340] request_id=abc123 tier=standard token_bucket_remaining=0; throttle=1; upstream_pool=hotpath-usw2-1 queue_pos=53
[1890012342] request_id=def456 token_bucket_remaining=0; throttle=1; autoscaler_decision=NO_ACTION (cap_reached)
```

devon: quick mitigation options: 1) increase token refill and burst for standard tier, 2) temporarily bump max_per_zone, 3) route overflow to warmpool/latency-tolerant pool (lower-cost model variant). Which do we want?

maria.ops: prioritize customer impact -> route overflow to warmpool and bump per-zone cap. Devs: can we change token bucket refill live?

jordan: yes but careful — increasing refill for all could cause cost spike; we can target only hotpath pool for now. Command to adjust: ```sh
redwoodctl rate set --tier standard --pool hotpath --refill 2.5 --burst 10
```

sre-jon: I'm going to temporarily relax max_per_zone. Executing: ```sh
redwoodctl autoscale set --region us-west-2 --max-per-zone 6 && redwoodctl autoscale force-scale --region us-west-2 --target-nodes 12
```

incident-bot: action logged by sre-jon at 1890012500.

beth: started routing overflow to warmpool (latency-tolerant). Monitoring customer errors.

jordan: after adjustments, 429s dropped by ~70% in next 2m. Queue length falling to ~20. CPU/GPU utilization shifting to warmpool.

maria.ops: keeping token bucket change targeted. We'll revert refill to 0.8 and burst 2 once steady.

devon: root cause notes so far: 1) PR 7842 reduced per-zone cap without traffic pattern eval; 2) token-bucket settings were too strict for sudden bursty traffic (burst capacity insufficient); 3) autoscaler didn't have an emergency override to bypass cost caps for high error rates.

sre-jon: creating incident page and setting status to "degraded" for affected endpoints. I'll notify account teams for impacted customers.

incident-bot: created incident INC-2026-338 and channel #inc-1890012345 at 1890012600.

beth: quick note for customers: posting to status page now with ETA 1h while we stabilize.

jordan: follow-ups to file: revert risky PR or add traffic gating, add emergency autoscale override, make token-bucket defaults adaptive to short-term spike, add alert for autoscaler_policy_blocked.

maria.ops: agreed. I'll own the postmortem; assign to devon for autoscaler fixes and to jordan for rate config improvements.

devon: temporary rollback plan: revert PR 7842 and add a canary rollout gating for next change.

sre-jon: handoff: I'm taking the on-call for the next hour to watch the scale and routing. Maria, assign postmortem tasks and I'll follow up with deployment notes.

maria.ops: thanks. Handoff noted. :white_check_mark: We'll keep this thread updated with timeline and customer comms.

incident-bot: last update 1890012920 - throughput recovering, warmpool handling overflow, incident status: stabilizing.
